We are offering a fully funded 3-year PHD position at Salzburg University.

Title: Human-Centered Responsible AI

- Various backgrounds eligible, among others the interplay between HCI and AI

- Start in October 2026

- Application until Sep 9th 2026

Here you can find more information:

The University of Salzburg invites applications for a fully funded pre-doctoral position (75%, three years) within the Doctoral School Plus (DSP) Human-Centered AI: From Data & Algorithms to Interfaces. The successful candidate will join an interdisciplinary research environment that combines expertise in Artificial Intelligence, Human-Computer Interaction, Data Science, Geoinformatics, Privacy Engineering, and Governance to advance the scientific foundations of Human-Centered AI.

Dissertation Topic

Human-Centered Responsible Artificial Intelligence: Interdisciplinary Foundations, Methods, and Human-AI Interaction

The doctoral project investigates how interdisciplinary theories, research methods, and interaction design approaches can be integrated to understand, design, and evaluate Human-Centered Responsible AI systems.

The project explores topics including Human-AI Collaboration, Explainable AI, Human-in-the-Loop systems, AI Literacy, Fairness, Transparency, Trustworthy AI, Responsible AI, and Human-Centered Design.

The successful candidate will contribute to developing conceptual frameworks, conducting empirical studies, designing interactive AI systems, and publishing results in leading international conferences and journals in Human-Computer Interaction and Artificial Intelligence.

Responsibilities

The successful candidate will:

- Conduct independent doctoral research within the DSP research programme

- Design, develop, and evaluate Human-Centered AI systems

- Conduct interdisciplinary empirical research using qualitative, quantitative, and mixed-method approaches- Collaborate with researchers from different scientific disciplines

- Publish research results at leading international conferences and in peer-reviewed journals

- Participate actively in DSP activities, including colloquia, workshops, retreats, and international summer schools

- Contribute to teaching and supervision activities within the Department according to university regulations

We Offer

- A fully funded three-year doctoral position (75% employment)

- An outstanding interdisciplinary research environment

- Access to state-of-the-art Human-Computer Interaction and AI research laboratories

- Close supervision by internationally recognized researchers

- International research collaborations and conference participation

- An excellent publication-oriented doctoral education

Admission Requirements

Applicants should hold (or complete before the start of the contract) a Master's degree (or equivalent) in one of the following disciplines:

- Human-Computer Interaction

- Computer Science

- Artificial Intelligence

- Geoinformatics

- Data Science

- Cognitive Science

- Psychology

- Software Engineering

- Digital Design

- Related disciplines with a strong methodological background

The successful applicant is expected to fulfil the admission requirements for the relevant doctoral programme at the University of Salzburg.

Desired Qualification

Experience in one or more of the following areas is advantageous:

- Human-AI Interaction / Collaboration / Explainable AI / Responsible AI

- Human-Computer Interaction, User Experience Research

- Artificial Intelligence incl. supervised, unsupervised, or reinforcement learning

- Generative AI and Large Language Models

- Experimental Design / Qualitative / Quantitative Research Methods

- Statistical Data Analysis

- Programming skills (e.g., Python, JavaScript, C#, or comparable languages)

- Interactive System Development

- Good communicative skills in English, both in writing and speech

Application

Applications should be written in English and include the following documents:

- cover letter describing your motivation

- a CV

- the Master thesis or equivalent

- a list of publications (if existent)

- a brief description of your envisaged research

- contact details of up to three references
